Screen artifacts are various web pages and forms within a digital interface, each serving specific functions. The "Shopping Cart" screen artifact, identified by the ID 'cart_empty', is an empty shopping cart page with the title 'Shopping Cart'. This page can be accessed through the URL 'http://localhost:7770/checkout/cart/'. Another screen artifact, labeled 'category', represents the 'Electronics' category listing, accessible via the URL 'http://localhost:7770/electronics.html'. The 'home' screen artifact, titled 'One Stop Market', serves as the store homepage, which can be reached at 'http://localhost:7770/'. Additionally, there is an advanced search form, which allows users to perform detailed searches within the system. A customer login form artifact is also present, enabling users to log in and access their accounts. a11y
The term "a11y" is an abbreviation for accessibility, a concept that pertains to the design of products, devices, services, or environments for people with disabilities. It encompasses various features and elements aimed at enhancing usability for individuals who may have visual, auditory, physical, speech, cognitive, or neurological disabilities. A critical aspect of accessibility involves the use of screen readers, which ensure that users can navigate and interact with digital content effectively. The term "a11y" is also used to describe accessibility-related elements and is often associated with improving the user experience for people with disabilities by making technology more inclusive and usable. Additionally, "a11y" can refer to an organization dedicated to accessibility, an abbreviation for accessibility features, an accessibility label, and an accessibility-related element or initiative. In the context of web development, "a11y" is a term related to accessibility and usability. The term is closely tied to accessibility features for web elements, which are designed to enhance the user experience for individuals with disabilities. Accessibility features for web elements include attributes and elements that facilitate interaction and navigation for users with disabilities. These features are essential for ensuring that web content is accessible to everyone, regardless of their abilities.<SEP>Accessibility features for web elements<SEP>[a11y] is a term related to accessibility features.

The term "menu item role" further specifies this concept, emphasizing its application within a menu structure. bbox_px refers to the pixel coordinates of a bounding box, which can also be described as bounding box coordinates in pixels or simply bounding box coordinates. This term specifically denotes the position of a bounding box in terms of pixel values, often used in image processing and computer vision tasks. Bounding box coordinates in pixels provide a precise measurement of where a bounding box is located on a pixel grid, facilitating accurate object detection and tracking in digital images. Examples include the pixel coordinates of a button's bounding box, the bounding box coordinates for a general region, and the bounding box coordinates of various menu items such as "Sports & Outdoors" and "Sign-in Link". Additionally, bbox_px can also refer to the pixel coordinates of links and comboboxes, indicating the precise location of these elements within an image. Specifically, bbox_px encompasses the pixel coordinates of the product image container, the pixel coordinates of the menu item 'Beauty & Personal Care', and the bounding box coordinates of the 'Health & Household' menu item. The bounding box coordinates of the link element in pixels are also included in this definition.
